newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Australia builders urge infrastructure reform.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Australia builders urge infrastructure reform.

text.p: The Australian Constructors Association (ACA) called on Thursday for the government to replace the abolished infrastructure bonds scheme with a voucher system.
Under the scheme, the government would issue vouchers to be redeemed at the Australian Tax Office to offset the interest costs of major projects during the initial years of operation.
"Infrastructure is the main artery of our economy and if it is sub-standard, so too will be our economic performance," ACA president and Leighton Holdings Ltd chief executive Wal King told reporters.
King said a voucher system costing the government A$200 million annually would support A$5.56 billion in infrastructure development each year.
He did not provide details of how the system would work.

The Australian government announced on February 14 that it would introduce legislation into parliament to abolish the infrastructure bonds scheme, which has helped to fund projects such as Sydney's M2 Motorway and Victoria's City Link project.
Treasurer Peter Costello said at the time the scheme would be abolished because of the ease with which it could be exploited for tax minimisation.

"There would be no issue of using the vouchers for tax minimisation in the way that's been possible for the infrastruture bonds scheme," Vince FitzGerald, who directed the preparation of a report recommending the scheme, told reporters.
The report prepared by the Allen Consulting Group found the advantages of the voucher system would include:
-- reasonable incentives to help private sector projects overcome the problem of long-term projects accumulating large losses in the early years of construction;
-- value for money for tax payers;
-- certain and controllable costs for the government;
-- low transaction costs and simple administration; and
-- preventing the government making political commitments to specific projects.
King said he hoped the May 13 federal budget would contain some measure to replace the infrastructure bonds scheme.
The former Labor government announced the infrastructure bonds as part of its 1992 strategy to boost the then ailing economy.
Costello effectively ended the scheme last September, telling the Development Allowance Authority to accept no more applications. -- Canberra Bureau 61-6 273-2730
